title: Green Lane Retail — integration draft notes
body:
Context: Green Lane is a mid-market retail chain (210 stores, EU + UK HQ). They're evaluating Redwood for product search/assistant features and personalized recommendations. Primary ask is tight latency for search + vector recall and private deployment in Azure EU regions (Dublin/Frankfurt).

Call notes (2026-02-10 sync - Maya Thompson, Ethan Ruiz):
- Maya (Head of Data): wants embeddings-based product search to replace current Elasticsearch rerank stage. Target: 95th perc latency for search end-to-end <= 150ms.
- Ethan (Platform): mandates customer-managed VNet + KMS integration, SOC2/ISO references required, and support for their internal SIEM ingest.
- Concerns: catalog churn (SKU changes every 10-15 minutes), large product images and metadata, GDPR PII handling for user queries.
- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~30 QPS, peak ~220 QPS during promos; average request size small (several tokens) but recall + re-rank multiplies downstream work.
- Offline batch embedding pipeline already exists (Spark). They want option to switch between precomputed vectors and on-the-fly embeddings for newly added SKUs.

High-level requirements (raw):
- Deployment: private control plane (Redwood Private) in Azure EU with VNet peering and customer-managed vault (Azure Key Vault/HSM).
- Data residency: EU-only, logs forwarded to their SIEM, retention policy 30 days default.
- Model options: prefer open weights (cost reasons) — recommended: 7B-13B instruction-tuned models for retrieval-augmented tasks; for rerank may want a 13B quantized variant.
- Embeddings: 768–1536 dim acceptable; want vector similarity latency (ANN+host) 20–50ms p95.
- Throughput & autoscaling: handle bursts to 220 QPS with warm standby capacity; need predictable cold-start behavior (SLA for spin-up < 90s).
- Observability: token-level cost heatmaps, per-route latency breakdown, early-warning alerts for quality regressions (precision@k drop).
- Rollout policy: blue-green or canary with automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model under overload.

Gotchas / risks we flagged: 
- Catalog churn will invalidate caches; prefix/KV caching helps for prompt-based chat but less for pure embedding lookups. Need to propose either near-real-time index update process or a hybrid (precompute + delta on-the-fly).
- Vector store cold rebuilds during promotions could spike CPU/GPU; recommend throttled index updates + backpressure to frontend.
- Azure SKU constraints: H100 not available in their target region; A100 + multi-instance can work but cost & model selection change. Need to map model quantization profiles to available GPU SKUs.
- PII: users sometimes paste order IDs/emails — discuss automatic PII stripping or customer-side client redaction. Legal asked about log redaction: we should provide options and sample retention configs.
- Licensing: they prefer open models, but some best-performing weights have restrictive licenses — include a short note in SOW about license tradeoffs.

Immediate action items (internal):
- [SE-1] (Assignee: Priya) Draft capacity estimate for 200–250 QPS peak with A100 (single-region) and alternative with mixed H100 (if available). Include cost-per-1000-queries est. Due: 2026-02-20.
- [SE-2] (Assignee: Samir) Prepare short tech-deep slide (10 slides) explaining private deployment architecture: VNet peering, KMS flow, logging pipelines, SIEM integration example. Due: 2026-02-17.
- [ENG-1] (Assignee: Avery) Prototype embedding latency test harness using a representative product catalog (50k items) and evaluate ANN latency and recall under catalog churn. Use Faiss/Annoy/ScaNN sims. Due: 2026-02-24.
- [CS-1] (Assignee: Liam) Send follow-up email with proposed timeline, post-demo next steps, and NDA link. Also include checklist for security docs they requested. Due: 2026-02-12 (sent tentative).
- Create initial SOW + cost model draft for review (tag: SOW-GreenLane).

Questions to resolve (open):
- Can Green Lane accept a multi-region fallback (EU primary, US read-only backup) or strict EU-only? (Legal requirement vs availability).
- How aggressive can we be with caching TTLs given SKU churn frequency? Need sample churn trace from their side (request from Maya).
- Preferred embedding dim and whether they want vector quantization on store side (opportunity to reduce memory but could impact recall).

Suggested pitch points for next call (tech):
- Show demo of hybrid embedding approach: precompute + delta ingest with minimal recompute window.
- Cost comparison: hosted vs dedicated vs private (focus on predictable peaking cost and reserve capacity benefits).
- Explain graceful degradation: routing to smaller quantized model + ranked fallback.

Notes to self (messy):
- Consider adding small prototype with a 30-minute promotion simulator to stress test reindexing.
- If Azure H100 not in region, quantify perf gap A100->H100 for our recommended 13B model.
- Ask infra for a short runbook template for customer-managed KMS onboarding.

Next scheduled touchpoints:
- Tech deep-dive demo (1.5h) w/ Maya + Ethan + infra xfer folks — propose 2026-02-18 10:00 CET.
- Executive business sync (30m) — late Feb (TBD).

Bottom line (summary for sales): Green Lane likes Redwood's observability and rollout story. Their constraints (EU residency + catalog churn + tight latency) push us toward a private deployment with tuned batching and a hybrid embedding strategy. Need capacity numbers and security artifacts to move to SOW.
